description.narrative: " This is a FY02 operation that should proceed with processing towards the end of this fiscal year ONLY if significant progress is made in moving to redundancy payments to surplus civil servants. It would be a single tranche operation, with conditionality building on civil service reform (particularly reduction in size of civil service), enhancements to the government's accounting and financial management system, and public expenditure rationalization. The first two areas are supported under the Civil Service Modernization Credit, and successful implementation of this operation would ""prepare"" this part of the project. The third area should build on recommendations in the recent Public Expenditure Report. In my view, existing budgetary allocations for this operation (at least in large part and completely with regard to the associated supervision budget), should be relocated largely to the substantially under-funded supervision budget for the Civil Service Modernization Project. Keeping the allocation as it is now makes it ""ripe"" for those looking to squeeze budget, and it makes sense to at least do a gross realignment of resources at this point to protect the overall allocation for the Yemen budget. There will need to be very careful crafting of the rational for the operation around one-time fiscal costs of adjustment (severance payments), because the medium term macro framework projects a budget surplus for the next several years. It should be noted that in FY00, the previous country economist charged over $50,000 towards this operation. As a result, the operation will always come up with a ""flag"" of expenditures prior to the PCD of over the regional guidelines."
